note: motivation and definitions
text: 3 Introduction 3.1 Motivation Neuroimaging experiments result in complicated data that can be arranged in many different ways.

note: motivation and definitions
text: So far there is no consensus how to organize and share data obtained in neuroimaging experiments.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Even two researchers working in the same lab can opt to arrange their data in a different way.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Lack of consensus (or a standard) leads to misunderstandings and time wasted on rearranging data or rewriting scripts expecting certain structure.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Here we describe a simple and easy to adopt way of organising neuroimaging and behavioural data.

note: motivation and definitions
text: By using this standard you will benefit in the following ways:

note: motivation and definitions
text: ● It will be easy for another researcher to work on your data.

note: motivation and definitions
text: To understand the organisation of the files and their format you will only need to refer them to this document.

note: motivation and definitions
text: This is especially important if you are running your own lab and anticipate more than one person working on the same data over time.

note: motivation and definitions
text: By using BIDS you will save time trying to understand and reuse data acquired by a graduate student or postdoc that has already left the lab.

note: motivation and definitions
text: ● There is a growing number of data analysis software packages that can understand data organised according to BIDS.

note: motivation and definitions
text: ● Databases such as OpenfMRI.org accept datasets organised according to BIDS.

note: motivation and definitions
text: If you ever plan to share your data publicly (nowadays some journals require this) you can minimize the additional time and energy spent on publication, and speed up the curation process by using BIDS to structure and describe your data right after acquisition.

note: motivation and definitions
text: ● There are validation tools that can check your dataset integrity and let you easily spot missing values.

note: motivation and definitions
text: BIDS is heavily inspired by the format used internally by OpenfMRI.org.

note: motivation and definitions
text: While working on BIDS we consulted many neuroscientists to make sure it covers most common experiments, but at the same time is intuitive and easy to adopt.

note: motivation and definitions
text: The specification is intentionally based simple file formats and folder structures to reflect current lab practices and make it accessible to wide range of scientists coming from different backgrounds.1

note: motivation and definitions
text: 3.2 Definitions Throughout this protocol we use a list of different MRI related terms.

note: motivation and definitions
text: To avoid misunderstanding we clarify them here.

note: motivation and definitions
text: 1 For review of other data organization standards in neuroimaging see Appendix. －4－ 1.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Dataset - a set of neuroimaging and behavioural data acquired for a purpose of a particular study.

note: motivation and definitions
text: A dataset consists of data acquired from one or more subjects, possibly from multiple sessions.

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: Subject - a person or animal participating in the study.

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: Session - a logical grouping of neuroimaging and behavioural data consistent across subjects.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Session can (but doesn't have to) be synonymous to a visit in a longitudinal study.

note: motivation and definitions
text: In general, subjects will stay in the scanner during one session.

note: motivation and definitions
text: However if a subject has to leave the scanner room and then be re-positioned on the scanner bed, the set of MRI acquisitions will still be considered as a session and match sessions acquired in other subjects.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Similarly in situations where different type of data is obtained over several visits (for example fMRI on one day followed by DWI the day after) those can be grouped in one session.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Defining multiple sessions is appropriate when several identical or similar data acquisitions are planned and performed on all -or most- subjects, often in the case of some intervention between sessions (e.g., training).

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: MRI acquisition - a continuous uninterrupted block of time during which an MRI scanner was acquiring data according to particular scanning sequence/protocol.

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: Data type - a functional group of different types of MRI data.

note: motivation and definitions
text: In BIDS we define four data types: func (task based and resting state functional MRI), dwi (diffusion weighted imaging), fmap (field inhomogeneity mapping data such as field maps), anat (structural imaging such as T1, T2, etc.) 6.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Task - a set of activities performed by the subject that aim at eliciting changes in the brain.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Tasks are usually accompanied by stimuli and responses, and can greatly vary in complexity.

note: motivation and definitions
text: For the purpose of this protocol we consider the so-called “resting state” a task.

note: whether a task was one acquisition is a fact of the experiment
text: In context of MR, a task is always tied to one MRI acquisition.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Therefore, even if during one acquisition the subject performed multiple conceptually different behaviours (with different sets of instructions) they will be considered one (combined) task.

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: Event - a stimulus or subject response recorded during a task.

note: onset and duration are the first two columns
text: Each event has an onset time and duration.

note: motivation and definitions
text: Note that not all tasks will have recorded events (e.g., resting state).

note: motivation and definitions
motivation and definitions
text: Run - an uninterrupted repetition of an MRI acquisition that has the same acquisition parameters and task (however events can change from run to run due to different subject response or randomized nature of the stimuli).

text: －6－ 4 File Format specification 4.1 Imaging files Imaging data are stored using the NIfTI file format, preferably compressed NIfTI files (.nii.gz), either 1.0 or 2.0 version.

note: about the conversion tool
text: Imaging data should be converted to the NIfTI format using a tool that provides as much of the NIfTI header information (such as orientation and slice timing information) as possible.

note: about the conversion tool
text: Since the NIfTI standard offers limited support for the various image acquisition parameters available in DICOM files, we also encourage users to provide additional meta information extracted from DICOM files in a sidecar JSON file (with the same filename as the .nii[.gz] file, but with a .json extension).

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: 10 Multi-site or multi-center studies This version of the BIDS specification does not explicitly cover studies with data coming from multiple sites or multiple centers (such extension is planned in BIDS 2.0.0).

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: There are however ways to model your data without any loss in terms of metadata.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: － 30 － 10.1 Option 1: Treat each site/center as a separate dataset.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: The simplest way of dealing with multiple sites is to treat data from each site as a separate and independent BIDS dataset with a separate participants.tsv and other metadata files.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: This way you can feed each dataset individually to BIDS Apps and everything should just work.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: 10.2 Option 2: Combining sites/centers into one dataset Alternatively you can combine data from all sites into one dataset.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: To identify which site each subjects comes from you can add a "site" column in the participants.tsv file indicating the source site.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: This solution allows you to analyze all of the subjects together in one dataset.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: One caveat is that subjects from all sites will have to have unique labels.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: To enforce that and improve readability you can use a subject label prefix identifying the site.

note: advice on multi-site studies
text: For example sub-NUY001, sub-MIT002, sub-MPG002 etc.

note: labels are [a-zA-Z0-9]+
text: Remember that hyphens and underscores are not allowed in subject labels.
